title: The Last Day: raised and weighed
hookLine: the resurrection, the reckoning, the garden and the fire
carry: an atom's weight of good will be seen

lines: THE ONE WHO MADE IT FIRST.
cards: Tradition says a man in Mecca picked up an old bone, crumbled it in his hand, and asked the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ a mocking question. Who's going to bring this back to life once it's rotted away?
The Qur'an records the question, and the answer that comes back is very short: the one who made it the first time will make it again.
That exchange sits near the end of Surah Ya Sin, and tradition links that surah with the dying and the dead.

teach.b: The word for it is akhirah, the hereafter, the life that comes last. The Qur'an keeps setting it beside dunya, this near world, the one we're in now. Belief in the Last Day has four movements.

First, the resurrection. The bodies of the dead are raised, the bone in the man's hand included. The answer in Ya Sin argues from the first creation: making something again is no harder than making it at all.
Second, the reckoning. Every life is laid open.
Surah az-Zalzalah, a short surah about the earth shaking, ends with two lines: "And whoso doeth good an atom's weight will see it then, And whoso doeth ill an atom's weight will see it then."
Nothing is too small to count, in either direction. Third, the two homes.
The Qur'an describes a garden, with rivers, shade and peace, and a fire. It describes both vividly, and hides neither. Fourth, the One behind it.

teach.h: MERCIFUL, AND MASTER OF THE DAY.
teach.b: In the opening surah, al-Fatiha, Allah is called the Merciful and the master of the Day of Judgment in the same breath. Mercy and reckoning sit side by side. And this is why the Last Day sits among the six.
For Muslims, it gives the ordinary day its weight: the kind word, the shortcut not taken, the atom of good nobody else saw.

how: Belief in the Last Day is the fifth article of faith; Muslims recite al-Fatiha, which names Allah as master of the Day of Judgment, in prayer, and Surah Ya Sin may be read for the dying and the dead.

s: only big deeds count on the Last Day
Surah az-Zalzalah says whoever does good, or ill, an atom's weight will see it.
the opening surah names Allah as Merciful and master of the Day of Judgment together
mercy and reckoning sit side by side in the same short prayer.
the Qur'an describes only the fire, not the garden

games.q: a man crumbles an old bone and asks, who will bring this back to life? what is the Qur'an's answer?
o: the one who made it the first time.
games.why: in Surah Ya Sin, the answer is the one who produced it at first: making again is no harder than making.

practice: Think of meeting Him, or, if that isn't your language, of your life being seen whole.
Bring up one small good thing from this week, a door held, a message answered kindly, and let it be seen; then one small harm, and let that be seen too, without arguing.
If you pray, you can recite the opening surah slowly, with its two names, the Merciful and master of the Day; if not, just rest in being seen.
